summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/10)

data.turoyo: Yabo, mtaláf u+săwalàno, basyo! Gmaḥtat ruḥux ʕal u+săwalàno.’ Omar, ‘Ooo k̇urem, Ăla lo+kəmzabanne, u+săwāl lo+kəmzabanne.’
data.translation: Dad, sell off this livestock, enough already! You are putting yourself out because of this livestock’. He says, ‘Ooo, my boy, by God I won’t sell them. The livestock, I won’t sell them’.
data.ref: MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/10

rationale: First II Imperativ box and disposal sense 2; retain the father's refusal, which establishes the intended action.

summary: I talifi describes perishing soldiers. I gtulafno with overt aḥ ḥayayḏi at 28/101 differs from objectless ktulafno at 28/107; the latter's German reflexive does not supply an unspoken Turoyo object.
II contrasts animate destruction with one livestock-disposal Imperativ. The reply's sell verb grounds the disposal reading, but does not establish that mtaláf always lexically means sell.
II Detransitive at 91/4 has livestock affected by wind, storm and cold, without an agent. This is already filed and is not evidence for a new form.
29/219 gmitaləf has a vocalic discrepancy from existing gə-mtaləf. Retain II active semantically pending confirmation, rather than inventing Detransitive morphology.
Searches tulafno, mtal and matlaf found the known examples and no separate collocation to duplicate.
Is II mtaláf conventionally dispose of/sell off in this dialect, or a contextual hyperbole? The proposed sense deliberately says disposal, with selling as the contextual realization.
Does I accept general transitive destroying beyond the life-object construction? Preserve the inherited ??? for that claim.
Check gmitaləf at 29/219 against the existing gə-mtaləf spelling before drawing a diathesis contrast.
The matching III army passage is cited prs 31/15 but supplied as PrS 15/26. Verify the numbering system before changing its reference.
